meta.title: Zakat calculator
meta.description: Calculate zakat maal, income zakat, and zakat al-fitr in yen or rupiah with adjustable gold, rice, and exchange rates. Everything is calculated on your device.

title: Calculate your zakat in a minute
description: Nisab follows 85 grams of gold and the rate is 2.5 percent. Adjust the gold price, rice price, and exchange rate to today's values. Nothing you enter is saved.

settings.rateHint: Manual rate, default 1 JPY = Rp105. Check today's rate before paying.

maal.title: Wealth held for one lunar year
maal.description: Gold, silver, savings, receivables you expect to collect, and trade goods, minus debts due now.
maal.belowNisab: Your net assets are below the nisab. Zakat maal is not obligatory, but sadaqah is always welcome.
maal.aboveNisab: Your net assets reach the nisab. Zakat maal is due.
maal.dalil: Take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them (At-Tawbah 9:103). The 2.5 percent rate and the gold nisab follow the hadith on zakat of gold and silver narrated by Abu Dawud.

income.title: Zakat on salary and professional income
income.description: Enter your gross income. Nisab is 85 grams of gold per year; many scholars also allow deducting basic needs first.
income.belowNisab: Your annual income is below the nisab, so income zakat is not obligatory.
income.aboveNisab: Your income reaches the nisab. Zakat of 2.5 percent is due.
income.dalil: O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned (Al-Baqarah 2:267). Income zakat is paid monthly or yearly at 2.5 percent, by analogy with zakat on wealth.

fitrah.title: Zakat al-fitr before Eid prayer
fitrah.description: One sa of staple food, about 2.5 kg of rice, for every member of the household, including infants.
fitrah.dalil: The Messenger of Allah made zakat al-fitr obligatory, one sa of dates or barley, for every Muslim, free or slave, male or female, young or old (Bukhari and Muslim).

result.label: Zakat due
result.disclaimer: This calculator is a guide. For complex cases, ask the mosque imam or a trusted scholar.
